_comment: Documented ENSO teleconnections per Westfalia sourcing origin. 'el_nino_effect' is the expected effect of EL NINO; La Nina is broadly opposite but not symmetric, so the dashboard does not auto-invert it. 'confidence' reflects how well established the teleconnection is in the literature, NOT certainty for any given event. 'supply_tier' (primary/secondary/tertiary) weights the origin in ranking. Most origins have a single 'lag_months' pathway; where an El Nino peak hits two distinct stages (e.g. Michoacan's fruit-on-tree AND its main bloom) a 'pathways' array carries each, and the top-level lag_months/mechanism/impact are kept for backward compatibility. 'watch_window' is human prose; 'watch_months' is the machine-readable (MM-DD) version used in ranking. 'signal_effect' is the short phrase for the WHAT TO WATCH one-liner (per-pathway when pathways exist). Literature-based, not yet validated against our own rainfall data — see Phase 2 in climatology_project_outline.md.

origins.name: Michoacán / Jalisco
origins.watch_window: year-round — always at a sensitive stage
origins.mechanism: Suppressed summer monsoon and a more pronounced canícula during the Jun-Oct wet season.
origins.impact: Moisture stress during sizing of fruit already on the tree; potential downward shift in the size curve on the current harvest.
origins.signal_effect: moisture stress during sizing of the current crop

pathways.mechanism: Suppressed summer monsoon and a more pronounced canícula during the Jun-Oct wet season.
pathways.impact: Moisture stress during sizing of fruit already on the tree; potential downward shift in the size curve on the current harvest.
pathways.signal_effect: moisture stress on fruit sizing now — risk of a smaller size curve on the current harvest

pathways.mechanism: Drought stress during bloom reduces fruit set. The Sep-Feb Normal bloom — the main crop — overlaps the forecast El Niño peak.
pathways.impact: Reduced set on the Normal bloom carries into the Nov 2027-Apr 2028 harvest. At ~80% of near-term US supply, this is the largest single forward exposure in the origin mix.
pathways.signal_effect: the Sep-Feb Normal bloom is setting the 2027-28 main crop into the El Niño peak

origins.name: Sonsón, Antioquia
origins.mechanism: Reduced Andean rainfall and elevated temperatures. At 2,475m, clear-sky dry spells also raise radiative frost risk and páramo fire risk.
origins.impact: Colombia's Sep-Jan main crop overlaps the forecast El Niño peak, so drought stress lands on fruit currently sizing and being harvested — not only on a future crop. The Dec-Mar dry signal then carries into sizing for the Apr-Jul traviesa.
origins.signal_effect: drought stress on the main crop now sizing and being harvested
origins.confidence: high on drought, moderate on frost

pathways.mechanism: Reduced Andean rainfall and elevated temperatures during the Sep-Jan main crop harvest.
pathways.impact: Water stress on fruit currently sizing and being picked; the forecast El Niño peak lands inside the main harvest window.
pathways.signal_effect: drought stress on the main crop now sizing and being harvested

pathways.mechanism: The Traviesa bloom occurs mid-year, roughly 7-9 months before its Mar-Aug harvest.
pathways.impact: Drought stress on the current Traviesa bloom carries into the Apr-Jul 2027 crop.
pathways.signal_effect: the Jun-Aug Traviesa bloom is setting the Apr-Jul 2027 crop

pathways.mechanism: The Principal bloom occurs Jan-Mar — precisely when Colombia's El Niño drought signal is strongest — roughly 8-10 months before its Sep-Feb harvest.
pathways.impact: The Jan-Mar 2027 main bloom falls in the peak drought window of a very strong event. This sets the Sep 2027-Feb 2028 main crop and is Colombia's largest single exposure.
pathways.signal_effect: the Jan-Mar 2027 Principal bloom sets the 2027-28 main crop in peak drought

origins.name: Eje Cafetero / wider Antioquia
origins.mechanism: Same Andean drought signal at somewhat lower elevation.
origins.impact: Colombia's Sep-Jan main crop overlaps the forecast El Niño peak, so drought stress lands on fruit currently sizing and being harvested — not only on a future crop. The Dec-Mar dry signal then carries into sizing for the Apr-Jul traviesa.
origins.signal_effect: yield stress across the 220-grower contract base

pathways.mechanism: Same Andean drought signal at somewhat lower elevation, during the Sep-Jan main crop harvest.
pathways.impact: Water stress on fruit currently sizing and being picked across the 220-grower contract base.
pathways.signal_effect: yield stress across the 220-grower contract base now sizing and being harvested

pathways.mechanism: The Traviesa bloom occurs mid-year, roughly 7-9 months before its Mar-Aug harvest.
pathways.impact: Drought stress on the current Traviesa bloom carries into the Apr-Jul 2027 crop.
pathways.signal_effect: the Jun-Aug Traviesa bloom is setting the Apr-Jul 2027 crop

pathways.mechanism: The Principal bloom occurs Jan-Mar — when the El Niño drought signal is strongest — roughly 8-10 months before its Sep-Feb harvest.
pathways.impact: The Jan-Mar 2027 main bloom falls in the peak drought window, setting the Sep 2027-Feb 2028 main crop.
pathways.signal_effect: the Jan-Mar 2027 Principal bloom sets the 2027-28 main crop in peak drought

origins.name: Lambayeque (northern coast)
origins.mechanism: Strong Niño 1+2 warming drives extreme rainfall on the northern Peruvian coast. 1998 and 2017 produced severe flooding in Piura and Lambayeque.
origins.impact: Field access, root disease, and road/packhouse logistics disruption. Infrastructure risk more than yield risk.
origins.signal_effect: flood risk to fields, roads, and packhouses

origins.name: Cañete Valley / Áncash (central coast)
origins.mechanism: Warm coastal winter reduces chill accumulation and suppresses flowering induction. Central coast sees far less El Niño rainfall than the north.
origins.impact: Reduced flowering carries into the March-September 2027 harvest. A very strong El Niño peaking OND 2026 sits directly on the Aug-Oct flowering window — the 2027 Peruvian crop is being set now, 7-13 months before it reaches arrivals.
origins.signal_effect: warmer winter may suppress flowering that sets the 2027 crop

origins.name: Monobamba, Junín (cloud forest)
origins.mechanism: Amazon-facing eastern Andean slopes typically run drier during El Niño — opposite sign to the Peruvian coast.
origins.impact: Moisture stress in cooperative-sourced high-altitude fruit.
origins.signal_effect: moisture stress in high-altitude cooperative fruit
origins.confidence: low-moderate — Monobamba sits in a transition zone and the signal is less well established than the coastal one
